item.text:
**The serving result supports a bounded integration finding, and the next step should be a $0 check while a stored replay is writing.** It does not yet establish that a running page stays current as the library changes.

The saved results support the four dated `/library` comparisons, the three January closings, the still-open question, and the seven cards rendered from a different API dataset. The comparison is against `bundle.library` on the same store, so it checks the HTTP path and serialization; it is not an independent check that the bundle itself represents every store value correctly. The page check is headless, and the test used no Idea configuration or embedding calls. [SERVE-RESULT.md](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/page-contract/SERVE-RESULT.md:3), [serve-check.txt](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/page-contract/serve-check.txt)

Two observations matter to the product, even though this test did not establish them as defects against a written requirement. The page loads the library once at startup and silently retains the embedded snapshot if that read fails. It also retains or clamps the selected date when a live dataset arrives; the test showed that this can initially display only two questions from the seven-question library. These behaviours limit any claim that the page shows the *current* library. [bootstrap.js](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/poc/ui/src/bootstrap.js:246), [library.js](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/poc/ui/src/components/library.js:173)

**Next test:** replay stored answers into a new scratch store, with the API and page reading it at controlled pauses: before the first completed day, during a later judging round, immediately after day completion, and after a due-day closing. Compare each response with the last completed day and inspect what an already-open page shows versus a freshly opened page. Use the real writer and read path, isolated files, and a transport that refuses any request without a stored answer.
